symbioteFindings: info signature-changed src/scan.ts#scanFolder: scanFolder changed its signature compatibly; existing users keep working (1 user, 0 untouched · 2 test users, 1 not updated)

findings.text: A UTF-8 byte-order mark (BOM) at the start of `.locignore` is not removed. `readFile(..., 'utf8')` keeps U+FEFF, so the first pattern becomes '﻿pattern' and never matches. Git removes the BOM from .gitignore. A file saved by an editor that adds a BOM therefore quietly loses its first rule.

Only ENOENT and EISDIR are treated as 'no .locignore'. Any other read error is rethrown, for example EACCES on an unreadable `.locignore`. scanFolder then rejects, and the CLI (src/cli.ts:12) dies with an unhandled rejection and a stack trace instead of a `loc: ...` message.

The test is named '* and ? do not match /', but it only checks `/` against `*` (`a/b`). No assertion checks that `?` does not match `/` (e.g. `ignored('x/z', false)` should be false for `x?z`), so a `?` mapped to `.` would still pass.
Nothing tests the command's new `--no-ignore` flag (or that the command applies `.locignore` by default). The goal requires both, and no test runs the CLI at all.

The scanFolder tests only use any-depth patterns (`vendor/`, `*.gen.ts`). No scan test covers a pattern anchored to root, a `!` re-include, or a nested ignored folder. Through scanFolder, that leaves untested that walk() passes paths relative to root with `/` (which anchoring depends on) and that ignored folders are not entered.

blind.summary: I found no blocker or major defects; the change meets the goal. I checked each `.locignore` rule in the goal against `src/ignore.ts`: comments, blank lines, trailing spaces, CRLF, `*`, `?`, `**` in all three positions, anchored versus any-depth patterns, the trailing `/` for folders only, the last match winning, and that a file can't be included again under an ignored folder. All of them behave correctly, including `a/**/b` matching `a/b` and names containing newlines or emoji. `scanFolder` and the CLI use the matcher as the goal says. `ignore: false` and `--no-ignore` turn it off, and `.locignore` itself is counted like any other file. The defects left are minor: a byte-order mark (BOM) at the start of `.locignore` is not removed, an unreadable `.locignore` crashes the command, and three tests are missing or don't check what their names say.
